records.region: Southern Honduras: upper valley, José Cecilio del Valle/Nacaome reservoir, Nacaome plain and the inner Gulf of Fonseca outlet.
records.candidate_name_role: bounded middle/lower river identity; provisional representative candidate only
records.material_pending_reason: Independent readable evidence for the selected upper western bend and return into the southgoing collector beside the cloud-obscured enlarged-water/junction setting is missing.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The named Nacaome river/reservoir and lower collector are supported, with Río Grande del Sur retained as the distinct upstream branch description. The complete selected group remains unresolved because one upper geographic through-link is unestablished.
records.completion_scope: The bounded source comparison is recorded, but full selected geographic correspondence remains incomplete at the stated upper through-link. Lower naming observations do not count as a completed whole-selection representative identity.
records.supported_name_scope: The named Nacaome river/reservoir and lower collector are supported, with Río Grande del Sur retained as the distinct upstream branch description. The complete selected group remains unresolved because one upper geographic through-link is unestablished.

scope_limits: The upper selected bend/junction beside the partly cloud-covered enlarged-water feature is the one material geographic gap. Surrounding valley similarity alone does not close it.
Names Petacón, Grande de Reitoca and other labels present only in unavailable-source discovery are not adopted as evidence.
FONAC supplies the regional upstream branch and reservoir identity, not a legal registry name, exact source point or exact hydronym-transition boundary.
The coastal image supports the bay-side receiving setting, without adopting an unverified local bay label or extending the selection to the open Pacific.
Distinct upstream/lower names and an impounded passage do not themselves create a scope hold; the primary pending status arises from the real upper correspondence gap.

records.region: South-central Alaska: Marcus Baker Glacier, Glacier Fork and Lake Fork Knik River, lower Knik braided valley and Knik–Matanuska estuarine flats.
records.candidate_name_role: Bounded glacier and river-component identities only; no representative natural-river name established for the full ice-field-to-estuary composite.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The opening and upper modeled course traverse glacier ice, followed by separately named river and lake-margin components. Geographic correspondence is complete, but no single natural-river name is established for the whole selected composite.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Marcus Baker Glacier covers the mapped upper ice passage; Glacier Fork and Lake Fork Knik River cover their directly labeled selected component settings; Knik River covers the lower braided selected corridor. None is imposed as a natural-river name on all glacier, lake and terminal components.
records.completion_scope: Full selected geographic correspondence is complete at ordinary regional and corridor scale. The null name reflects glacier-and-lake naming scope, not inability to trace an exact present water thread. No further external acquisition is needed for this bounded pass.
records.supported_name_scope: Marcus Baker Glacier covers the mapped upper ice passage; Glacier Fork and Lake Fork Knik River cover their directly labeled selected component settings; Knik River covers the lower braided selected corridor. None is imposed as a natural-river name on all glacier, lake and terminal components.

scope_limits: The selected initial and upper modeled mainstem traverse glacier ice. Geographic coverage does not establish a named natural river, supraglacial channel or subglacial hydraulic route there.

The lake and foreland components are assessed as continuous geographic receiving settings. Present ice front, lake level, individual active braid and current flow are unverified and unnecessary for this geographic finding.
The separate source and rendered mainstem terminal positions occupy different parts of the shared lower receiving flats. They are described separately rather than moved or forced onto an exact bank.
A formal name-register entry, legal name boundary and Korean rendering were not verified.
The successfully acquired optional Esri middle view was never visually read; the lower view execution was interrupted without a confirmed outcome. Neither image is evidence.

Source originals and local orientation files were subsequently lost with the workspace. This record preserves completed observations from the actual reads; it does not assert that the files survive or that any source was reacquired.

records.region: Baja California, Mexico: interior arid tributary canyons, El Rosario receiving valley and the Pacific-shore endpoint.
records.geographic_disambiguation: El Rosario is directly attached to the lower watercourse in the municipal Relieve map. The hydrological study explains that this name follows the meeting of El Potrero and San Juan de Dios. Complete geographic correspondence connects the selected headward branch to this named lower system, without assigning El Rosario as a uniform name to every upstream part.
records.completion_scope: All 23 selected parts and intervening joins are covered by three overlapping photographic views and the retained municipal map. The direct lower El Rosario label and the state study’s tributary-to-El Rosario description support representative system identity. Upper part-level names remain bounded rather than being forced into a single scalar name.
records.supported_name_scope: El Rosario is directly attached to the lower watercourse in the municipal Relieve map. The hydrological study explains that this name follows the meeting of El Potrero and San Juan de Dios. Complete geographic correspondence connects the selected headward branch to this named lower system, without assigning El Rosario as a uniform name to every upstream part.

scope_limits: No part-level assignment of El Potrero versus San Juan de Dios is made for the chosen upper branch. Their existence as forming tributaries is supported by the prose; distinct component names do not defeat the representative identity.
No precise name-transition point, current bank, continuously open coastal mouth, present surface flow, tidal direction, irrigation operation or official source/mouth is established.
The historical municipal boundaries and hydrological synthesis dates are not claims about present administration or hydrological conditions.

A later local display bundle was interrupted without a confirmed returned image; no additional visual claim depends on that output. Earlier completed original acquisitions and actually inspected views remain the evidence.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
